title.narrative: Immediate food assistance for the affected population in Guantanamo, with emphasis on the 4 most affected municipalities and on the prevention of malnutrition of prioritized and most vulnerable group.

description.narrative: The action plan for the CERF allocation is based on a life-saving strategy and consists of providing in-kind food (1 kg of rice, 0.5 kg of pulses and 1 L of veg oil per family) during the first month of the emergency, supporting Cuban authorities in preserving the food security and nutrition of nearly 149,693 people in the 4 Guantanamo´s municipalities: Baracoa, S. Antonio del Sur, Imías, Maisí, that had been most affected by Hurricane Oscar. Special emphasis is placed on the food assistance for shock-affected population through social protection institutions enabled for the delivery of food daily rations. WFP will support the immediate delivery of food (rice, pulses, oil) as complement and support for the preparation of food in evacuation centers and other institutions set up such as communities’ canteens, children's day care centers, primary schools, maternity homes, family care systems, homes for the elderly, grandparents' homes, and other centers in the communities. Furthermore, will be guarantee one distribution round of the bimonthly WFP food module of rice, pulses and oil to y the most vulnerable groups and pregnant women in the same municipalities as a complement to the government's standard family basket.WFP provided tents and cooking utensils for the most affected families, mobile storage units, lighting equipment and pallets to restore local food storage. WFP will help increase the capacity of community kitchens to cook food through the purchase of non-food items to support people who have lost their homes. It will also support the immediate purchase of batteries and tires for government trucks to ensure the transfer and distribution of food. To ensure timely assistance, WFP used food and non-food items already pre-positioned in the country. WFP Cuba requires a total of US$ 1,120,000.00 from the CERF for this operation, which represents 11% of the total WFP operational action plan for this emergency.
